title: Why Paper Cuts Hurt So Much

sections.name: Why Paper Cuts Hurt So Much
lines: It's such a tiny cut. So why does it hurt this much?
Your fingertips are packed with more nerve endings than almost anywhere on your body.
And a paper's edge looks smooth, but up close, it's jagged, like a saw.
So it rips the skin, instead of slicing it cleanly.
The cut is so shallow it barely bleeds, so nothing seals it, and the nerve endings are left open to the air.
And every time you bend your finger, you pull the cut open again.
Cover it with a bandage, and the pain fades fast.
